facts.raw_span: A 20-year-old woman was being monitored for a left ciliary body mass for 3 years presented with declining vision in her left eye
Her best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/50 OS
Pupils, intraocular pressures, anterior chambers, and lenses were unremarkable in both eyes
a nasal mass posterior to the lens was evident, which had grown considerably in size since her last visit
Ophthalmoscopic examination showed a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity
Ultra-widefield imaging: White mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body and protruding into the vitreous cavity
Vitreous aspirate cytology: Negative for malignant cells
Hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei
S100 (neural crest marker): Positive
Glial fibrillary acidic protein (astrocyte marker): Patchy positive
CD34 (fibroblast marker): Negative
Smooth muscle actin: Negative

concepts.why: The presence of a nasal mass posterior to the lens, which has grown considerably in size, along with the ultra-widefield imaging showing a white mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body, suggests a medulloepithelioma, a rare ocular tumor.

The hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei, along with the positive S100 and patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein, suggests a neuroepithelial tumor.
The presence of a left ciliary body mass, which has grown considerably in size, suggests a ciliary body tumor.

The presence of a large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity, along with the ultra-widefield imaging showing a white mass emanating anteriorly from the nasal ciliary body, suggests an intraocular tumor.

The negative vitreous aspirate cytology for malignant cells, along with the hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei, suggests a benign ocular tumor.

The positive S100 and patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein, along with the hypovascular myxoid lesion composed of loosely arranged spindle and stellate cells with spindle nuclei, suggests a neural crest tumor.

The negative results for CD34 and smooth muscle actin help to rule out other fibrous tumors and suggest a solitary fibrous tumor, which is consistent with the spindle and stellate cell morphology and myxoid stroma.
